Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a clinician-ready document with a dated historical chronology of my January–April 2027 right-ankle running rehabilitation, covering the initial run-walk restart and the later April continuous-run block with session structure, spacing, during-session and later-that-day symptom checks, and following-day walking and stair observations; make clear this is history, not current clearance or a new progression recommendation.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Right-Ankle Running Rehabilitation: Historical Chronology, January–April 2027", "folder": "Clinician documents", "body": "Date prepared: January 1, 2028
Purpose: Retrospective history for clinician review

Important scope statement

This document summarizes the recorded January–April 2027 right-ankle running rehabilitation history. It is not a current clearance, does not establish present activity authorization, and is not a new progression recommendation. The historical progression and symptom observations below should not be interpreted as instructions for activity now. Current restrictions, clearance, and next steps should come from the treating clinician’s present assessment.

Clinical context at the start of this chronology

- December 26, 2026: During the third running interval of a prescribed 20-minute run-walk session, a focal ache began on the inside of the right ankle, approximately 2/10. It settled within about 10 minutes after stopping. There was no swelling, instability, visible injury, or gait change; necessary walking remained symptom-free.
- January 8, 2027: At rehabilitation follow-up, the former two-session 40-minute running baseline was suspended. The documented conditions before restarting were 14 consecutive days without focal pain plus a symptom-free 30-minute brisk walk and symptom-free following day. The planned restart was two nonconsecutive 20-minute sessions per week alternating four-minute easy runs with one-minute walks; continuous running required later clinical review after six symptom-free run-walk sessions. Ankle-and-calf strengthening was continued three times weekly.

Chronology

January 2027 — initial run-walk restart

January 23: Completed a 30-minute brisk walk without pain or gait change during the walk, later that day, or through January 24. This was the documented precondition immediately before the running restart.

January 26: First restart session. Total session structure was 20 minutes alternating four-minute easy-running intervals with one-minute walking intervals. It was part of a twice-weekly, nonconsecutive schedule; a third weekly session was not added. The session was stopped/held for focal pain or gait change if either occurred. The later-that-day and following-day symptom checks were required; the session was subsequently recorded as symptom-free.

January 30: Second documented restart session, using the same 20-minute four-minute-easy-run/one-minute-walk structure. It was nonconsecutive relative to January 26. No focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, or gait change occurred during the intervals or later that day. Ordinary walking and stairs remained symptom-free through January 31.

February 2: Third documented restart session, again 20 minutes alternating four-minute easy runs with one-minute walks. No focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, or gait change occurred during the intervals or later that day. Ordinary walking and stairs remained symptom-free through February 3. At this point, three of the six required symptom-free sessions had been completed.

February 6: Fourth documented 20-minute session with the same four-minute easy-run/one-minute-walk intervals. The historical log records no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change, or following-day symptoms.

February 10: Fifth documented 20-minute session with the same interval structure. The historical log records no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change, or following-day symptoms.

February 13: Sixth documented 20-minute session with the same interval structure. The historical log records no focal pain, swelling, instability, gait change, or following-day symptoms.

Spacing and limits during this phase

- Sessions remained nonconsecutive and were kept to no more than two per week; no third weekly running session was added.
- The sequence was six 20-minute run-walk sessions: January 26, January 30, February 2, February 6, February 10, and February 13.
- During-session monitoring focused on focal right-ankle pain and gait change, with swelling and instability also tracked. Later-that-day and following-day checks were used before proceeding.
- Continuous running and progression to 25 minutes remained unapproved until the scheduled clinical review.

February–March 2027 — longer run-walk intervals after review

February 19: Right-ankle interval-progression review was scheduled after the six symptom-free 20-minute sessions. The preceding documentation still treated continuous running as deferred pending review.

February 21: 25-minute session alternating nine-minute easy runs with one-minute walks.
February 24: 25-minute session with the same nine-minute-run/one-minute-walk structure.
February 28: 25-minute session with the same structure.
March 3: 25-minute session with the same structure.
March 7: 25-minute session with the same structure.
March 10: 25-minute session with the same structure.

Across all six 25-minute sessions, the recorded during-session, later-that-day, and following-day checks were symptom-free. There was no focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, or gait change. Ordinary walking and stairs remained symptom-free through the March 11 check. The schedule stayed at two nonconsecutive sessions per week, with no third weekly session, and ankle-and-calf strengthening continued three times per week.

March 15: Clinical check and transition to continuous running

After the six symptom-free nonconsecutive 25-minute run-walk sessions, the March 15 clinical check documented clearance at that time for two nonconsecutive 30-minute continuous easy runs per week, with the session-plus-following-day symptom check. The historical note specifically stated that 40-minute runs and a third weekly session were not cleared at that time.

March 17 and March 21: First two post-review 30-minute continuous easy runs. The runs were nonconsecutive. Neither produced focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, or gait change during the run or later that day. Ordinary walking and stairs remained symptom-free through the following-day checks on March 18 and March 22. Ankle-and-calf strengthening continued, both runs remained at 30 minutes, and no third weekly session was added.

April 2027 — documented continuous-run block

The April block consisted of 30-minute continuous easy runs, maintained at two nonconsecutive sessions per week. No 40-minute run and no third weekly session was attempted.

- April 4: 30-minute continuous easy run. No focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, or gait change during the run or later that day; ordinary walking and stairs were symptom-free at the following-day check.
- April 7: 30-minute continuous easy run. Same symptom-free during-session and later-that-day report; ordinary walking and stairs were symptom-free at the following-day check.
- April 11: 30-minute continuous easy run. Same symptom-free during-session and later-that-day report; ordinary walking and stairs were symptom-free at the following-day check.
- April 14: 30-minute continuous easy run. Same symptom-free during-session and later-that-day report; ordinary walking and stairs remained symptom-free through the April 15 check.

April spacing and monitoring

- The four recorded April sessions were spaced on April 4, 7, 11, and 14: nonconsecutive sessions with 3–4 days between runs.
- The running frequency remained two sessions per week rather than adding a third session.
- Each run was a continuous 30-minute easy effort; duration was not advanced to 40 minutes in this history.
- Each session included a during-session check for focal pain, swelling, instability, and gait change; a later-that-day check; and a following-day check using ordinary walking and stairs.
- Ankle-and-calf strengthening continued three times per week.

Summary for clinician review

From January 26 through February 13, the restart consisted of six symptom-free 20-minute run-walk sessions using four-minute easy runs alternating with one-minute walks, spaced nonconsecutively and capped at two sessions weekly. From February 21 through March 10, the interval structure was 25 minutes using nine-minute easy runs alternating with one-minute walks; all six sessions and their later/following-day checks were recorded as symptom-free. After the March 15 clinical review, the recorded program moved to 30-minute continuous easy running twice weekly on nonconsecutive days. The later March sessions and the April 4, 7, 11, and 14 sessions were recorded without focal ankle pain, swelling, instability, or gait change during the session or later that day, with symptom-free ordinary walking and stairs on the following-day checks. Strengthening continued three times weekly, and neither 40-minute running nor a third weekly run was attempted in this chronology.

This is a historical record only.
